vp15.reference: Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.15, Wilson translation, Āditya genealogy
vp15.finding: Names Aditi and Kashyapa as the parents of the twelve Adityas, including Sakra; Kashyapa is son of Marichi and Aditi daughter of Daksha.

av310.finding: Ekastaka bears Indra and is called mother of Indra and Soma and daughter of Prajapati. Does not name Indra’s father.

sb6187.finding: Paulomi (Saci) bears Jayanta, Rishabha and Midhusha to Indra.

rv1086.finding: Indrani is Indra’s consort; no link to the Buddhist Suja is asserted.

rv418.finding: Narrates unusual birth and conflict with a father but does not unambiguously name the parents in the reviewed translation. No inferred Tvashtr parent edge.

sakka.reference: G. P. Malalasekera, Dictionary of Pāli Proper Names, s.v. Sakka, sections on family, epithets, office and Indra
sakka.finding: Sakka is a repeatable office; dictionary distinguishes Buddhist Sakka from Vedic Indra. Four daughters named; biological families are not transferred across the comparison.

suja.reference: G. P. Malalasekera, Dictionary of Pāli Proper Names, s.v. Sujā, DhA i.269–279 and DA iii.716–717
suja.finding: Separates human wife, crane, potter’s daughter and Vepacitti’s daughter across rebirths; mother of the asura birth unnamed.

magha.reference: G. P. Malalasekera, Dictionary of Pāli Proper Names, s.v. Magha, J i.207 and SA i.267
magha.finding: Jataka identification with Bodhisatta conflicts with commentary identification. Do not flatten into a unique historical identity.

kulavaka.reference: G. P. Malalasekera, Dictionary of Pāli Proper Names, s.v. Kulāvaka Jātaka 31
kulavaka.finding: Sudhamma, Citta, Nanda and Sujata are human wives of Magha; first three attain heaven through meritorious work.

sudhamma.reference: G. P. Malalasekera, Dictionary of Pāli Proper Names, s.v. Sudhammā 3
sudhamma.finding: A human donor reborn in heaven; the hall is not a separate person.

susima.reference: G. P. Malalasekera, Dictionary of Pāli Proper Names, s.v. Susīma 5, S i.217; SA i.262
susima.finding: Son of Sakka and deva general; probable identity with another Susima is not resolved.

matali.reference: G. P. Malalasekera, Dictionary of Pāli Proper Names, s.v. Mātali, D ii.268 and Jātaka accounts
matali.finding: Charioteer and father of Sikhandi; Jataka identity changes by story, so attendant is not a biological child of Sakka.

pancasikha.reference: G. P. Malalasekera, Dictionary of Pāli Proper Names, s.v. Pañcasikha, D ii.263–268
pancasikha.finding: Musician and intermediary, spouse of Bhadda Suriyavaccasa; office and previous lives vary.

timbaru.reference: G. P. Malalasekera, Dictionary of Pāli Proper Names, s.v. Timbaru, D ii.266, 268

sudha535.reference: G. P. Malalasekera, Dictionary of Pāli Proper Names, s.v. Sudhābhojana Jātaka 535, J v.382–412
sudha535.finding: Four daughters; Hiri marries the reborn Kosiya. Earlier human descent of the five deities must not be flattened into heavenly biological parents.

siri.reference: G. P. Malalasekera, Dictionary of Pāli Proper Names, s.v. Sirī 1–2
siri.finding: Dictionary distinguishes the daughter of Sakka from a Sirī daughter of Dhatarattha.

sn113.reference: Saṃyutta Nikāya 11.3, Dhajagga Sutta, Thanissaro translation
sn113.finding: Standards of Sakka, Pajapati, Varuna and Isana; Sakka still experiences fear. Does not attest hurling a vajra.

jaanus.reference: JAANUS, s.v. Taishakuten, iconography at Tōji
jaanus.finding: Japanese name and script; protector of Buddhism; Tōji elephant mount and single-pronged vajra. No separate biography inferred.

samguk.reference: Iryeon, Samguk yusa, book 1, Gojoseon entry
samguk.finding: Hwanin glossed 帝釋; Hwanung descends with three unspecified seals and wind, rain and cloud officers. Bear becomes woman after twenty-one days. Tangun reigns 1500 years and becomes mountain god aged 1908.

yuhuang.reference: Gaoshang Yuhuang benxing jijing, upper scroll, Qingwei tiangong shentong pin 1, Jingde and Baoyueguang narrative
yuhuang.finding: Names king Jingde and queen Baoyueguang; dream conception, princely manifestation, abdication and cultivation. These are manifestation-specific parents, not borrowed Indra genealogy.

heissig.reference: Walther Heissig, The Religions of Mongolia (1980), pp. 49–50
heissig.finding: Discusses Qormusta, competing Iranian and Indra influences, and an equation with Esrua/Brahma; no single secure transmission route.

eravana.reference: G. P. Malalasekera, Dictionary of Pāli Proper Names, s.v. Erāvana 1, DhA i.273f; SnA i.368f
eravana.finding: A deva assumes an elephant form; previous animal birth distinct from deva body. No biological relation to Indra inferred.

vissakamma.reference: G. P. Malalasekera, Dictionary of Pāli Proper Names, s.v. Vissakamma, Vissukamma, D ii.180; DhA i.272; J iv.325
vissakamma.finding: Divine architect summoned by Sakka; office with different story-specific previous lives, not imported Hindu genealogy.

sunetta.reference: G. P. Malalasekera, Dictionary of Pāli Proper Names, s.v. Sunetta 4, A iv.103f
sunetta.finding: Ancient teacher, distinct from three other dictionary namesakes; cultivation of loving-kindness does not bring liberation.

rohini.reference: G. P. Malalasekera, Dictionary of Pāli Proper Names, s.v. Rohinī 2, DhA iii.295ff
rohini.finding: Sister of Anuruddha; heavenly favourite of Sakka after death; not the nun or Hindu namesakes.

raji.reference: W. J. Wilkins, Hindu Mythology, Vedic and Puranic, chapter VII, pp. 61–62
raji.finding: Indra acknowledges Raji as father after military aid. A political or honorary acknowledgement, not birth genealogy.

marici-brahma.reference: Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva LXVI, Ganguli translation, six spiritual sons of Brahman
marici-brahma.finding: Marichi named among Brahman’s spiritual sons. Spiritual origin is not biological maternity or fatherhood.
